title: v2.13.0 — Steady Hands
body:
Online play stops flinching:
- The Resyncing… toast no longer fires when nothing is wrong — a move landing, a skill check resolving or a rematch starting is no longer mistaken for a board that has drifted; a board that genuinely is behind still gets repaired within a few seconds
- A build the server is too new for now gets a clear Update required card naming both versions, instead of an endless search for a game it would never be given
- The server keeps an eye on its own housekeeping and reports its health honestly, so the connection test can tell you when it is full or falling behind
- A broad hardening pass underneath: cleaner refusals, tidier logs and steadier behaviour under load

title: v2.12.2 — Spring Cleaning
body:
Under-the-hood maintenance release:
- A full internal polish pass over the whole codebase, plus a sweep of small fixes it surfaced
- Positions pasted as FEN now keep their move number, refuse a malformed side-to-move, and show the check highlight right away
- Esc no longer acts on things hidden behind a blocking overlay, and sound switched on mid-game now works fully
- Smoother long sessions: less busywork per frame during live games and when browsing past moves

title: v2.12.1 — No Loitering
body:
Quality-of-life sweep for online play:
- Idle openings now resolve themselves: no first moves for a minute aborts the game, and going silent right after the opening auto-resigns — both players see the countdown ticking on the idle side's strip
- Manual board flip (F) works in online games again, and your skill-check aim follows the flip correctly
- Pick your server under Options › Online: Official or Custom, with a live connection test button
- Opponent drawings now appear the instant they land, and reconnects restore the exact shared-marks state
- Open PGN tells you what went wrong when it can't open — and hides itself when there is nothing saved yet

title: v2.12.0 — Two-Step
body:
Two fresh ways to win a capture — the shootout is now a four-way draw:
- Whack-a-Mole: the captured piece dives into a pit, then pops from a ring of glowing holes — tag it before it ducks away for good, and keep your trigger honest: three whiffed shots and it walks
- Your attacker keeps the gun out for the whole hunt and swings it after your crosshair; land the last shot and it takes the square still holding it
- Miss, and the mole climbs back out of the pit, stitches itself together, and has an opinion about your aim
- Combo: a strip of arrow prompts flies in — hit each one in order with Arrows/WASD or the on-screen pad; three wrong inputs and the dance is over
- Keep the chain clean and the strip catches fire
- Your opponent watches your whole check live on their board, painted in spectator blue — every shot, every whiff, every wrong arrow
- A full sound kit for both: telegraphs, pops, ricochets, a hit ladder that climbs with your streak, and a taunt you will not enjoy

title: v2.11.0 — Rules of Engagement
body:
Cleaner shared play and a readable news feed:
- Shared board drawings are now moderated — prohibited hate symbols are blocked before they reach your opponent, and a blocked mark turns red for you with a heads-up
- Hide your opponent's shared marks entirely with the new HIDE toggle — flip it in the in-game SIGNALS row or under Options › Online
- The News card now carries the full history — every past update, expandable and scrollable, with an unread badge for what you haven't read

title: v2.10.0 — Battle Station
body:
The in-game screen joins the Command Rail:
- Board plate, player strips, and right rail fully redesigned
- Share your board drawings with your opponent — flip SHARE in SIGNALS
- Quick chat: pick a line and your queen says it on their board
- Opening names show live in the shot log
- Auto-queen toggle for instant promotions (the skill check still fires)
- Black pieces wear a rim light — readable on every square
- Games with no moves played now abort: no winners, no losers

title: v2.9.0 — Command Rail
body:
The main menu got rebuilt end to end:
- New left nav rail with a sliding crosshair
- Revolver-cylinder time picker — click the center pin for a random time control
- Right rail with your profile, recent matches, and this news feed
- Fresh gunmetal sounds throughout
- The menu shootout now spills out from under the rails

title: v2.8.0 — Substation
body:
Groundwork for what's coming, plus one handy tweak:
- Open PGN now opens the game in your system's default app
- Rebuilt the app's screen plumbing so new screens (profile, friends, and more) can arrive faster

title: v2.7.0 — Field Repairs
body:
A repair-and-polish sweep:
- Live games now save reliably even if you close or leave mid-move
- Browse your move history during a live game with the arrow keys; Home/End jump to the ends
- Skill-check dials and crosshairs scale cleanly at every window size
- Draw results show the real reason — stalemate, repetition, fifty-move, insufficient material — instead of "by agreement"
- The Windows portable build ships its license and attribution files; macOS builds no longer hide your games inside the app bundle

title: v2.6.0 — Tunnel Vision
body:
Distraction-free play:
- New Focus mode collapses the in-game UI down to just the board — press H or click the arrow in the board seam
- Choose what stays on screen: a thin time line on the board edges, the full player strips, or nothing at all — Options › Focus mode
- A game result auto-expands the UI; Esc steps back out before it offers to resign

title: v2.5.0 — Full Auto
body:
A big frame-rate boost:
- The board only repaints what actually changes, so idle and menu frame rates climb sharply
- New Performance readouts — FPS, 1% lows, and render time — in Options › Performance
- Fixed a bug where a game could run past 0:00; a flagged clock now ends the game

title: v2.4.3 — Reinforcements
body:
More control at the board:
- Press and hold "Give 15 sec" to pour extra time onto your opponent's clock, up to the starting time (a tap still gives a single 15s)
- Volume sliders now tick as you drag them, with a gun-cock ratchet while you hold to give time
- Windows: edge-resize, drag-to-snap, and taskbar-aware maximize now work on the window

title: v2.4.2 — Failsafe
body:
Stability fix:
- Fixed a crash on Windows when a game ended, caused by non-ASCII text in saved games or nicknames
- Nicknames are now limited to standard ASCII so they always render correctly

title: v2.4.1 — Hold the Line
body:
Online reliability fixes:
- Online games now reliably save to PGN, including on checkmate and if you close mid-move
- Steadier reconnection — a game interrupted by a dropped connection is recovered from the server

title: v2.4.0 — Live Rounds
body:
A full sound overhaul:
- Every piece has its own move sound, and a distinct gun on a won capture check — pawn revolver, knight hand-cannon, bishop lever-action, rook shotgun, queen blunderbuss, king ray-gun
- Skill-check cues: a ding as the dial opens, a tick in the sweet spot, and a win/miss sting
- A two-stage low-time heartbeat that speeds up as your clock runs down
- Announcer killstreaks and result voices, plus castle doors, undo rewind, and board-flip whoosh
- All audio is now cleanly licensed with full attribution

title: v2.3.6 — Sound Check
body:
An early taste of the sound overhaul:
- First pass at per-piece move sounds, expanded in full in v2.4.0

title: v2.3.5 — Briefing
body:
Docs:
- Documented the F11 fullscreen shortcut in Help and the README

title: v2.3.4 — Second Wind
body:
Online play polish:
- Rematch now works and swaps sides correctly — rooms stay alive while you're on the result screen
- Windows window controls: work-area maximize, F11 fullscreen, minimize, and double-click the title bar
- A piece you're dragging is no longer hijacked when your opponent's move lands
- The material bar now counts promotions
- Rematch offers reach you on the menu, and even after a quick restart, via a drop-in banner
- Notifications are now a tidy stacked queue

title: v2.3.3 — Safety Catch
body:
Bug fix:
- Fixed a bug that could quit you to the main menu mid-game when clicking to select a piece

title: v2.3.2 — Open Line
body:
Online, out of the box:
- Downloaded desktop builds now connect to the public Chess Shootout server automatically — no server address to type in (you can still override it in Options › Server)

title: v2.3.1 — Steady Hands
body:
Smoother browsing:
- The games list stays smooth with hundreds of saved games
- New performance readout in the window bar: FPS and live ping — toggle in Options › Performance
- A friendly "Already in a game" message replaces the old raw code

title: v2.3.0 — Quick Draw
body:
The Shootout mechanic arrives:
- Every capture and promotion now fires a fast, skill-based minigame — win it and the move lands; miss and that move is locked for the turn, with no turn lost
- Two checks: the Wheel, a timing dial, and Steady-Aim, a crosshair tracing a shrinking target; the more material at stake, the tougher the check
- Fully server-adjudicated online and takeback-proof, and your opponent watches your attempt live
- Every hit and miss is saved into the game's PGN and shown in review — and still imports cleanly on chess.com and Lichess

title: v2.2.1 — Momentum
body:
Scrolling that feels right:
- Click-drag to scroll any list — the move log, history, options, pickers, and Help
- Flick to fling with kinetic momentum, or grab the scrollbar thumb directly

title: v2.2.0 — Heft
body:
Pieces you can feel:
- Grabbed pieces now tilt and swing with real inertia while you drag, then rotate upright and glide onto their square on release
- A hard flick can spin a piece a full turn; it respects your reduce-motion and effect-intensity settings

title: v2.1.2 — Quartermaster
body:
Behind the scenes:
- A one-command update path for the online server, so fixes reach you sooner

title: v2.1.1 — Supply Line
body:
Behind the scenes:
- Build-pipeline fix so server updates ship cleanly

title: v2.1.0 — Garrison
body:
Behind the scenes:
- The online server moved to a hardened, containerized setup for steadier matches and quicker updates

title: v2.0.2 — Fair Fight
body:
A fairer online game:
- Disconnects are handled fairly — a game that never recovers aborts with no winner if it had desynced, otherwise the waiting player wins
- A new amber "resyncing" connection state keeps both players in sync
- Fixed recapture premoves, a replaying "FIRST BLOOD" callout, rematch side-flip, and nickname saving
- On packaged builds, window resize and the minimize/maximize buttons work again

title: v2.0.1 — Warpaint
body:
Windows fix:
- Country flags and emoji now render correctly on Windows instead of showing as blank squares — shipped as pre-rendered art, which also shrinks the download

title: v2.0.0 — Muzzle Flash
body:
A full visual overhaul:
- A brand-new Chess Shootout look — clean at rest, chaos in the moments: gun-toting pieces, announcer callouts, screen-shake, and killstreaks
- Redesigned board, pieces, player strips, modals, and menus with new fonts and art
- A capture arsenal: muzzle flash, tracer, impact, bullet hole, sparks, board-shake, and ragdoll
- Match-found VS reveal, searching radar, on-board reconnect overlay, and draw/takeback banners
- A match-grouped games browser replaces the old file picker

title: v1.0.0 — First Blood
body:
Chess Shootout launches:
- Play chess locally or online with live matchmaking, reconnect, resign, draw offers, takebacks, and rematches
- Standalone desktop downloads for Windows, macOS, and Linux
- An Options menu with a configurable games folder; games auto-save to PGN
- The gun-fight theme: pieces that shoot, killstreak callouts, and a menu shootout backdrop
